_doc: New-defect-CLASS discovery per cold audit. Mahmood's 'how far from finished' metric: the rate at which each audit finds a genuinely NEW class of error (vs recurrences of classes already diagnosed). A bending curve = approaching the class ceiling; the arithmetic is beyond reproach (engine reproduced 23/23..25/25 across audits 24-26), so every remaining class is a DESCRIPTION failure (the data sits correct one layer down while the framing over-claims). Counts for audits 22-25 are the auditor's stated figures; audit 26 is this session's classification. Earlier audits (1-21) predate this explicit tracking.

new_classes: IRR-mistyping (first-event/mortality rate ratio typed as person-time incidence-rate ratio)
NOT_RUN-as-paywalled (access-outcome claimed while the full-text adapter never ran)
DETECTED-INVALID-BUT-PUBLISHED (a gate that detects failure and still renders the number is a caption, not a gate; disclosure is not suppression)
cross-module evidence-state drift (two modules assign contradictory states to one record)
UNKNOWN-aggregated-as-negative (unknown folded into the negative denominator)
composite-to-construct substitution (a cardiorenal composite promoted to an organ-specific 'CKD progression' claim)
estimand-gate inversion (an endpoint rule applied in opposite directions to included vs excluded evidence)
umbrella-intervention identity collapse (a heterogeneous intervention SET promoted to one named intervention)
reassurance-about-a-defect-that-is-itself-unverified (a 'this would not change X' claim asserted without computing it)
comparator-predates-our-included-trials (a benchmark that cannot cover trials published after it, presented as parity)
recurrences: unit-of-analysis violation published anyway (cluster-randomised crossover analysed as parallel = detect-and-render)
a check that cannot fire (census reports zero failures while a documented expected-failure passed)
audits.note: audit-26 classification is this session's assessment, not an auditor-stated figure; reassurance-unverified is the clearest new sub-class.

trend_note: new-classes-per-audit 22->26: 3, 3, 2, 1, 2. The curve is bending toward the class ceiling; recurrences now dominate each audit, which means the open problem is LANDING fixes on the served pages faster than an auditor re-finds them, not discovering the classes.
